item.title: It's a norm not to have a public holiday on a weekday if Fiji Day falls on a Saturday – Tikoduadua

item.content:encoded:
Fijians will not get an additional public holiday on Friday or Monday despite Fiji Day falling on a Saturday this year, with the Government saying the national celebration remains on 10th October.

While responding to a question from fijivillage News on why a public holiday has not been allocated on a weekday to allow people to participate in celebrations and promote patriotism, national pride and unity, Minister for Defence Pio Tikoduadua says Fiji Day celebrations is on Saturday this year, when most people do not work.

Insert: Tikoduadua on Fiji Day 5th Oct 26

The Minister says the main Fiji Day celebration will be held in Suva this Saturday, culminating with the Fiji Day military parade at Albert Park in the morning.

Tikoduadua launched Fiji Day Week 2026, saying the celebrations provide an opportunity for Fijians to celebrate independence, reflect on the country's history and recognise those who continue to contribute to the nation.

He says this year's Fiji Day Week focuses on building an inclusive Fiji for a better tomorrow.

Activities this week will include market stalls, community and public activities, a clean-up initiative and a history day at the Fiji Museum.

Tikoduadua says there will also be activities in other major centres, including Lautoka and Nadi, while visits to orphanages and homes for older people are among the initiatives planned.

He says different government ministries will also conduct activities focusing on some of the major challenges currently facing the country.

Tikoduadua says the Ministry of Health will focus heavily on HIV awareness, while Police will carry out counter-narcotics activities.

He says drugs and HIV are two major challenges affecting Fiji, and the independence day provides an opportunity for the country to come together in confronting these issues.

Tikoduadua says the Ministry of Defence is also looking at its role and at defence capabilities and mechanisms that could assist Police and other law enforcement agencies in keeping people safe.

He says the Ministry of Women and Children will also undertake social work as part of activities around Fiji Day.

Tikoduadua says while the celebrations are primarily planned around the activities of different ministries, the private sector also traditionally contributes towards Fiji Day activities.

Reflecting on Fiji's history, Tikoduadua says Fiji was ceded to Great Britain on 10th October 1874 and was administered as a British colony for 96 years before gaining independence on 10th October 1970.

He says independence gave Fiji the freedom to determine its own future, but that freedom also came with the responsibility to build the country, look after one another and leave a stronger Fiji for future generations.

Tikoduadua says Fiji has experienced many changes and challenges over the past 56 years, but the resilience of its people remains one of the country's greatest strengths.

He says Fiji Day Week is not only about looking back but also recognising the contributions of communities, young people, veterans, uniformed services, workers and families.

Tikoduadua says building Fiji is a shared responsibility, and while the Government has a role to play, every Fijian also has a responsibility.

He is encouraging people to participate in activities throughout Fiji Day Week, celebrate responsibly and reflect on what independence means to them.

item.title: Teachers deserve reliable systems and timely support - Radrodro
item.description: As Fiji celebrates World Teachers’ Day today, Education Minister Aseri Radrodro says the needs of teachers, students, schools and communities remain at the centre of the country’s education system. Radrodro says teachers deserve reliable systems and timely support, following the recent salary disruption affecting 134 teachers.
item.content:encoded:
As Fiji celebrates World Teachers’ Day today, Education Minister Aseri Radrodro says the needs of teachers, students, schools and communities remain at the centre of the country’s education system.

Radrodro says teachers deserve reliable systems and timely support, following the recent salary disruption affecting 134 teachers.

He says the Ministry is strengthening its payroll and human-resource systems, reviewing internal processes and tightening checks to prevent similar issues from happening again.

Radrodro says a review has also been carried out by senior officials, with recommendations now being considered.

He says the Ministry continues to work on reforms aimed at improving the quality, accessibility and effectiveness of education across Fiji.

Radrodro says the recently completed Education Commission review also provides important recommendations for the future direction of the education system, which the Ministry is carefully considering.

He says the Government’s responsibility is to ensure every child has access to quality education, every teacher is supported and every young person has the opportunity to reach their full potential.

Radrodro says education is not simply about today, but about preparing the next generation to lead, serve and build a stronger Fiji.

Meanwhile, students sitting the 2026 national external examinations have been urged to stay confident and focused, with the Fiji Year 8 Certificate Examination set to begin tomorrow.

A total of 19,141 Year 8 students will sit their examinations from tomorrow until Thursday at 718 centres.

A total of 8,561 Year 13 students will sit the Fiji Year 13 Certificate Examination from 27 October to 6 November at 174 centres, while 12,388 Year 12 students will sit their examinations from 11 to 23 November at 177 centres.

Radrodro says students should trust their preparation, manage their time well and give their best effort, reminding them that examination results do not define their future.

He also acknowledged teachers, parents and guardians for supporting students and encouraged them to provide patience, guidance and reassurance throughout the examination period.

item.title: MPs had no time to properly scrutinise Constitution Amendment Bill – Chaudhry
item.description: Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry has questioned the legitimacy of the Constitution amendment process, claiming it was rushed and MPs were not given enough time to properly read, analyse and debate the Bill. Chaudhry questioned why there was a need to rush the process after what he says was little action on constitutional reform during the Government’s three and a half years in office.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Labour Party Leader Mahendra Chaudhry has questioned the legitimacy of the Constitution amendment process, claiming it was rushed and MPs were not given enough time to properly read, analyse and debate the Bill.

Chaudhry questioned why there was a need to rush the process after what he says was little action on constitutional reform during the Government’s three and a half years in office.

He claims there must be an agenda behind the rushed process and says the Government made several mistakes in its haste.

Chaudhry also claims the Government treated the Supreme Court opinion as law without presenting a Bill to Parliament to convert the opinion into law.

He says they have challenged the legitimacy of the process from the beginning and intend to continue raising the matter as the process moves forward.

Chaudhry also criticised NFP Leader Professor Biman Prasad for supporting the Constitution Amendment Bill.

He referred to Prasad’s comments on 18th September that the NFP would not be part of any attempt to rush the implementation of a new Constitution, and described his subsequent support for the Bill as a turnaround.

Chaudhry says 38 MPs supported the Bill and claims Prasad’s support gave the Government the numbers it needed.

He also raised concerns about the amount of time MPs had to consider the Bill, saying the report was given to them late on Wednesday afternoon before Parliament sat throughout Thursday and into early Friday morning.

Chaudhry questioned when MPs had time to read, analyse and understand the Bill before it was tabled on Friday morning, saying it would have been impossible to have a meaningful debate in that timeframe.

He claims the lack of time for a full debate raises questions about the validity of the process.

The Bill has now been referred to a bipartisan parliamentary committee for 30 days to seek public views and prepare a report before the third reading.

Chaudhry says attention should also turn to the next general election, which he says Parliament has been told will be held before 6th February 2027 under the 2013 Constitution.
